text.card: The nearest millisecond pulsar: a neutron star 23 km across that turns 174 times a second.
text.introduction: PSR J0437−4715 is a neutron star 157 parsecs away, 1.4 times the Sun's mass in a ball 23 km wide. Its surface is near 250,000 K, with patches over a million.

notes: Its companion, a 0.22 solar-mass helium white dwarf on a 5.74-day orbit (Reardon et al. 2024), is not drawn
The maximum-likelihood regions are drawn, as in the paper's Figure 11; the same fit's radius for that single vector is 13.17 km, and the sphere uses the posterior median 11.36 km
